facts.claim: Recommendation systems can facilitate both algorithmic control and creative self-transformation.
facts.quote: Thus, recommendation systems can facilitate both algorithmic control and creative self-transformation, which calls for a theorization of this new cultural medium as a space of tension.

facts.claim: Users on the music recommendation website last.fm use recommender systems to examine and transform their own music taste.
facts.quote: User practices on the music recommendation website last.fm reveal that many users do not only utilize the website to receive guidance about music products but also to examine and transform an aspect of their self, i.e. their ‘music taste’.

facts.claim: A new algorithm can obtain simultaneous gains in both accuracy and diversity of recommendations without relying on any semantic or context-specific information.
facts.quote: By tuning the hybrid appropriately we are able to obtain, without relying on any semantic or context-specific information, simultaneous gains in both accuracy and diversity of recommendations.

facts.claim: A recommendation algorithm considering both the effects of similar and dissimilar users performs better than standard collaborative filtering for both accuracy and diversity.
facts.quote: Extensive analyses on three datasets, namely MovieLens, Netflix and Amazon, show that our method performs much better than the standard collaborative filtering algorithm for both accuracy and diversity.

facts.claim: Algorithmic filtering and adaptation of online content to personal preferences is often associated with a decrease in the diversity of information to which users are exposed.
facts.quote: The algorithmic filtering and adaption of online content to personal preferences and interests is often associated with a decrease in the diversity of information to which users are exposed.

research.angle: While algorithmic filtering is associated with decreased information diversity, these systems can also be designed to facilitate creative self-transformation and simultaneous gains in accuracy and diversity.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that while algorithms can narrow information exposure, they are also capable of being designed to increase diversity and support user self-cultivation.
research.caveat: The sources do not provide a definitive causal link between algorithmic curation and the narrowing of human aesthetic preferences, as some studies focus on design possibilities rather than outcomes.
